input.brief: Academic Wordbank: an internal phrasebank and academic vocabulary dictionary that mines rhetorical phrase frames with slots from licensed journal articles, so writers can see which phrases one journal characteristically uses

direction.name: The sentence is the layout
direction.idea: One short sentence, set at poster scale, is the composition. The trick that makes it an idea rather than a big headline: something from the subject sits inside the sentence where a word would be. A strip of photograph fills the gap between two words; a small live fragment of the product replaces the noun; the object the sentence names is pictured at the size of a letter. Write the sentence first, find the word that can be shown instead of said, and put the showing in its place. The reader completes the sentence with their eyes.
direction.composition: The sentence is four to seven words and runs as one or two full-width lines at 9–13vw. Inline with the type, on the baseline, sits one media slot: a rounded-rectangle or square frame exactly one line-height tall and two to three ems wide, holding a photograph or a looping crop. Above and below the sentence the screen is empty except for a small navigation line and one supporting sentence set small, both on the same left margin. Later sections repeat the grammar at smaller scale: each is a short statement on the left six columns with its proof (image, figure, list) on the right, so the page reads as a series of sentences with evidence. Generous vertical space (160px or more) between sections.
direction.typography: Display weight with real presence (medium to bold), tracking -0.03 to -0.05em, leading 0.95–1.0 so two lines sit close. The inline frame aligns to cap height and baseline exactly; set it with em units so it scales with the type.
direction.colour: A calm ground with ink at full contrast. The only colour comes from the photograph inside the sentence; if the palette has an accent, use it once, on the action.
direction.imagery: One strong, simple photograph that reads at small size (a face, an object, a texture, a horizon), cropped to a wide strip inside the sentence. The same image may open to full width in the next section, so the small slot feels like a window onto something larger.
direction.richness: The collision of big type and one live image inside it. Because there is only one image on the first screen, choose it with care and give it perfect alignment to the letters.
direction.pitfalls: The sentence must be short enough for two lines on a phone, where the inline frame drops to its own line between the two halves. Do not style one word differently to fake the device. Do not use more than one slot per sentence.

hero.name: Headline across two fields
hero.blueprint: The viewport is two flat fields meeting at exactly half height: paper above, one saturated colour below, with a hard edge and nothing drawn on it. A two-line headline in black-weight capitals at clamp(96px, 9.5vw, 150px), line-height 0.86, is centred across the seam and spans about 70% of the width, so line one stands on the upper field and line two is cut through its upper third by the seam. The type changes ink where it crosses: above the seam it takes the accent ink, below it a deep ink two steps darker than the lower field, as if submerged. Build it as two stacked copies of the same headline, one per ink, the first clipped with `clip-path: inset(0 0 50% 0)` and the second with `inset(50% 0 0 0)`. Wordmark top-left at 28px; up to four text links and the single action, a solid rectangular button, top-right. One supporting sentence at 20px in the paper colour is centred on the lower field, 56px above the bottom edge. The lower field continues for 30svh past the fold before the next colour begins.
hero.mobile: The same two fields with the seam at 46svh. The headline stays on two lines at 15vw, centred, still cut by the seam and still changing ink. Wordmark top-left and the action button top-right; the links drop into one menu word beside it. The supporting sentence sits on the lower field at 16px, centred, max 28ch, with 40px beneath it.
hero.headline: A statement of two to four words on two lines, up to about 10 characters per line, whose meaning the rising field acts out.

type.note: A tall American gothic taken from city signage, blunt and civic, over a plain public-service sans. Suits culture indexes, community projects, bars, sport clubs and local campaigns.

palette.name: Tobacco and olive
palette.note: Tobacco brown fills the page with bone type, and photographs stay in browns and ochre. One olive block holds the main text or the button, and a single ochre band may break the brown once.

motion.name: Colour by chapter
motion.description: Each chapter is its own full-bleed field of one palette colour, so the ground changes exactly at section edges as you scroll, never as a global recolouring of the screen. The only movement: the fixed header (or the one pinned element) takes the ink of the chapter beneath it, switching with a 300ms colour transition as each edge passes under it. Do not drive the page background from an observer: in blind tests a page recoloured mid-section, with a paragraph sitting on two colours, read as broken twice.

sections.name: Headline crossing onto a photograph
sections.blueprint: A white or pale ground. A photograph taller than it is wide, 720px wide (columns 7–12), sits flush against the right viewport edge with its top at 46% of the section's first screen and runs below the fold. The heading starts on the 32px left margin across columns 1–8: two lines of light-weight serif capitals at clamp(64px, 5.6vw, 88px), leading 1.04, the first line starting 34% down the screen and the second placed so that its right half runs onto the photograph's upper-left corner. Choose a picture whose upper-left quarter is pale enough for the ink, or set the second line twice, in the ink and in the paper colour, each copy clipped to its side of the photograph's left edge. Under the heading on columns 1–5, one paragraph of up to 25 words at 22px, leading 1.4. At the bottom-left a second, smaller photograph of 360×400px enters, cropped by the screen's lower edge, and on the next screen becomes the left half of a staggered pair with the large one. Nothing else is on the screen.
sections.mobile: The heading sits at 10vw on two lines on the 20px margin. The photograph becomes 75% of the width, flush right, and starts under the heading's first line so the second line crosses its top-left corner. The paragraph follows at 17px, then the small photograph at 50% of the width on the left margin.

sections.name: Object in front of type
sections.blueprint: Type and object share one space instead of sitting side by side. Three or four lines of display type, one or two words each, are stacked flush left at clamp(72px, 9vw, 150px) with leading 0.88, starting on the left margin and allowed to leave the right edge (white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden on the section). The lines step through tones of one ink: one at 45%, one at full strength, the rest at 18%. The object photograph, a cut-out or a studio shot blended with multiply, is absolutely positioned over the upper right of the stack at 40–46vw wide, rotated no more than 6 degrees and above the type in the stacking order, so it hides parts of three or four letters. Under the stack, in columns 8–12, a two-paragraph block at 20px gives the facts. The full-strength line is the heading; nothing sits above it.
sections.mobile: Type drops to 15vw and still runs off the right edge. The object sits at 78vw wide, overlapping the last two lines from below instead of from the right, and is cropped by the right edge. The facts block follows at full width and 17px.

sections.name: One verb at a time
sections.blueprint: Three to five full-bleed panels, each 100svh tall, stacked with no gap; each is one stage and holds one photograph covering it. In every panel a single word, the verb for that stage ('Cut', 'Fold', 'Stitch', 'Press'), is set at clamp(96px, 17vw, 300px), heavy and centred, inside a wrapper that is position: sticky; top: 50% and shifted up by half its own height. Because each word is sticky only within its own panel, it holds the centre of the screen while its photograph passes behind it, and is then pushed out by the next panel's verb. Use mix-blend-mode: difference in white, or one solid colour tested on every image. One sentence at 18px sits in the bottom-left corner of each panel over a neutral scrim limited to that corner. There is no separate heading: the verbs, read in order, are both the heading and the sequence.
sections.mobile: Panels stay 100svh, each photograph cropped to a vertical slice. The verb is 24vw, still sticky at the centre. The sentence sits along the bottom over a scrim at 16px, full width with 16px margins.

sections.name: Statement, table pushed right
sections.blueprint: A heading of four to six words spans the full width on two lines at clamp(40px, 4.5vw, 68px), left-aligned with its first line indented 3vw and leading 0.98. 96px below, the table is pushed into the right-hand five columns (8–12) and the left stays open. One plain word naming the table (offices, hours, rates) hangs at 14px in column 7, top-aligned with the first row. Each row is a three-part line at 15–16px with 26px between rows: the kind or day in the soft ink at the left of the measure, the place or service at 30%, and the address, time or price right-aligned, with a small arrow where the row links. Rows are separated by space only; every fourth row has 44px above it to form groups. In columns 1–4, bottom-aligned with the last row, one 4:5 photograph 22vw wide may sit alone. Holds 5–14 rows.
sections.mobile: Heading at 9.5vw without the indent. The table takes the full width at 16px; each row stacks the kind above the place, with the value right-aligned on the first line. The naming word is dropped because the heading already says it. The photograph follows at 60% width on the right margin.

sections.name: Wide heading, indented questions
sections.blueprint: A heading of three to five words at about 5.5vw runs from the left margin on one or two lines and is the only large thing in the section. 80px beneath it the questions begin, indented to start at column 5 and running to column 12, so the left third under the heading stays empty. Each question is a row at 22–24px in the regular weight with a chevron of two 2px strokes at the far right; rows are separated by 36px of space and no rules. Opening a row lays a tile of the one-step tone behind that row and its answer (24px padding, extending 24px beyond the text on both sides) and shows the answer at 17px with a 48ch measure. Six questions. Nothing else shares the screen; the indent against the wide heading is the composition. Build with `<details>`.
sections.mobile: The heading sits at 10vw on two lines. Questions lose the indent and run full width at 19px with 28px between rows; the open row keeps its tone tile, now bleeding to both screen edges, with the answer at 16px inside it.

sections.name: Question at both edges
sections.blueprint: For a closing choice between two answers: book or ask, this date or that, the tasting or the tour. A flat field exactly 100svh tall in the darkest tone. The question is a two-line heading at clamp(110px, 11vw, 168px), leading 1.0, centred, about 54% of the width: line one with its cap line 32px under the field's top edge, line two with its baseline 24px above the bottom edge. The band of about 560px between them is empty except for one row at its optical centre: two solid rectangular buttons, each about 200×56px with its label at 18px in medium weight, their inner edges 120px either side of the centre axis, and between them, exactly on the axis, the word 'or' at 18px in the soft ink. 16px under the row, centred, one line at 16px in the soft ink says what happens after either choice. The type above and below closes the empty band, so it reads as held breath rather than a gap.
sections.mobile: The question drops to 18vw, still two centred lines, line one 32px from the top and line two 24px above the bottom. The buttons stack at the centre at 72% of the width, 12px apart, with 'or' between them and the line of explanation under the second.

sections.name: Invitation over a cropped name
sections.blueprint: Close and footer in one full-viewport field of the inverse colour. Upper third, columns 1–7: a two-line invitation at about 5vw, three to five words, with one filled rectangular button beneath it. At columns 10–12, top-aligned with the invitation, three or four social or contact links stacked at 16px. The wordmark fills the bottom of the screen at 26–30vw on one line, `white-space: nowrap`, heavier and larger than the viewport can hold: it is pushed down with `transform: translateY(30%)` so the bottom edge cuts through the letters, and a long name also runs off the right edge. `overflow: hidden` on the footer does the cropping. One row of credits and legal links at 13px sits directly above the wordmark's cap line, spread left and right. The cropped name must be recognisable from its upper two-thirds alone; test that it is.
sections.mobile: Invitation at 11vw on two lines at the top with a full-width button. Links follow as one row of words at 15px. The wordmark sits at 34vw at the bottom, cropped by both the bottom and the right edge, with the legal row above it at 12px.

references.name: bleibtgleich’26
references.idea: One thin vertical rule runs down the page and a tight bold grotesk sentence wraps around it, words stepping from one side of the line to the other.
references.hero: White page, black type. Content sits in a narrow band between 26% and 68% of the width. A 1px vertical rule drops from the top edge at 37% for two-thirds of the height. Left of it: a black blob avatar at the top, a tiny role caption at its foot. Right of it: a tiny location note at the top, the name in two lines of 90px medium grotesk at the bottom. The tagline continues below at the same size, flush to the band's left edge, running past the fold. The upper half is otherwise blank. The handle is split into two pale-grey words fixed in the bottom corners; a black menu pill sits top-right.
references.type: Akzidenz Grotesk Pro medium only, -0.05em tracking, line-height about 0.9. Two sizes: 90px (6.3vw) for every statement and 11-13px for captions and table rows, a 7:1 jump. Long words are hyphenated and stepped across lines on purpose.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #e4e4e4 #f2f2f2 — Black on white with no accent. Pale grey is used for the ghosted corner wordmark and a few small square tiles; tiny coloured rings inside those tiles are the only hue.
references.imagery: Almost none: a black blob avatar, a few 85px grey tiles each with a coloured ring, and a canvas dome of small tilted project thumbnails floating between two words.
references.layout: Everything hangs off one vertical axis at 37%: lines start either at the axis or one indent to its left, giving a stepped rag. Very wide white margins. Sections are separated by a full screen of white rather than rules or colour.

sections.description: A 90px sentence is typeset word by word around the vertical rule: one word ends just left of the rule, the next starts just right of it, and the following line is centred beneath both. Above the sentence a row of five 85px pale-grey squares, each with a small coloured ring at its centre, is spaced unevenly along one baseline, with a three-line 13px description under the second.

The heading first appears as one centred line near the bottom of an empty screen, then its two halves separate to the far left and far right edges at mid-height. In the gap a WebGL dome of fifteen or so small project thumbnails, mostly black and white, tilts in perspective like tiles on a sphere. Nothing else is on the screen.

The heading is broken into an ampersand alone in the left margin and two words stepped over three lines with a hyphen break and a growing indent. Below it a four-column table at 11px: year, site name, awarding body, award. Hairline rules sit under every row, columns align to the hero's band, and year groups are separated by a blank row.

The closing sentence is stepped over four lines with shifting indents, right of centre. To its left two tiny grey captions and an email address at 11px. Under it three 36px outlined circles with social initials, centred, then the handle at about 44px centred on the bottom edge with tiny legal text in the two corners.

steal: Draw one 1px vertical rule and typeset a large sentence around it, alternating words to either side so the line becomes the text's spine.
Split the logotype into two words, ghost them at about 10% grey, and fix one in each bottom corner of the viewport.
Leave the top half of the hero blank and start the name at 50% height so the headline runs off the fold and pulls the scroll.
references.media: No picture on the first screen, which is all type plus a small black mark. Pictures arrive later as a WebGL sphere of project thumbnails flanked by two words that slide apart on scroll, square tiles placed on separate grid cells with empty cells between them, hover thumbnails behind a text index, and one small image used as a glyph in a row of numerals; no video.
references.motion: A 2.5s progress counter runs although the page loaded in 1.5s, while a vertical line draws down with the role label at its tip. Lenis and 15 ScrollTriggers with nothing pinned: display lines rise by yPercent over 0.47s in-out at a 0.075s stagger, the globe's rotation is scrubbed across its 1178px block, the flanking words are pulled apart on a scrub, and underlines wipe in by background-size over 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.76,0,0.24,1).

references.name: CoffeeTech®
references.idea: Present an industrial roaster maker like a design brand: one enormous three-word statement on black, with the machine withheld until the first scroll, where it emerges from the dark.
references.hero: Near-black viewport with nothing but type. A centred three-line headline, one word per line, in Inter Medium at about 15vw with tight tracking; the first line starts a third of the way down and the last runs to within 35px of the bottom edge, its widest word spanning roughly 70% of the width. Cream letters; no subhead, no media, no hero button. Navigation is one quiet row: logo with a terracotta mark at left, four text links centred, then a filled terracotta 'Products' button with a grid icon, an outlined contact button and a language dropdown at right. The top third stays empty.
references.type: Inter throughout at weight 500. Display lines at 216px with -0.07em tracking and leading near 0.95 against 14px body, a jump of about 15 times. Secondary headlines near 10vw, intro paragraph around 26px. Section labels are tiny and wrapped in square brackets.
references.colour: #0d0e13 #e5e2dd #f3ece2 #c8603d #262629 — Blue-black and warm putty-grey sections alternate; cream type on dark, near-black on light. Terracotta appears only on the logo mark and the primary button.
references.imagery: Studio shots of roasters: a black machine barely lit against black after the hero, then white and black machines as cut-outs on pale-grey tiles. One warm founder portrait with a signature overlapping its edge; macro bean photos in small-radius cards.
references.layout: Outer margins of about 70px. A centred type poster on top, then an offset two-column intro, then a product grid pushed into the right two-thirds with its bracketed label alone in the left third. Oversized left-flush headlines open and close the lower page.

sections.description: Warm putty-grey band entered through a hairline. A portrait about 290px wide with 8px corners sits in the left third; a scrawled signature overlaps its bottom-right corner and spills onto the background. A seven-line paragraph at about 26px, medium weight, roughly 510px wide, begins at the horizontal midpoint, followed by a small underlined text link. No heading; the right quarter and the gap between the two elements stay empty.

A headline at roughly 10vw is flush to the left edge and clipped by the right, like a slow marquee. Below, a tiny bracketed label sits alone in the left third; the right two-thirds hold a two-column grid of pale-grey tiles about 400px wide with a small radius, each with a centred machine cut-out, the model name beneath and a tiny outlined pill for its category. The grid closes with a 64px underlined 'see all' text link with an arrow.

Back to blue-black. A cream contact headline at about 10vw sits hard against the left edge, far larger than anything near it. Underneath, the terracotta logo mark is enlarged to about 140px at left; four narrow link columns in small grey text run from 28% to 85% of the width; a pill-shaped back-to-top button sits at far right, with a thin legal row at the bottom.

steal: Let a three-word headline at about 15vw be the entire first viewport and withhold the product until the first scroll.
Photograph a dark product on a background matching the page colour so it appears to emerge from the page rather than sit in a box.
Overlap a handwritten signature onto the corner of a portrait so an about block feels signed rather than laid out.
references.media: The fold is type only; one scroll later a full-bleed low-key photograph of the roaster on matching black covers 76% of the screen, so the object floats out of the dark as the second beat of the hero. Below: a portrait with a signature over its edge, product renders contained on tinted tiles in a 2x2 grid, three 4:5 macro ingredient cards with the label docked bottom-left, and a blog slider; 25 images, no video, about 12.5px corners on card media.
references.motion: No entrance at all: the 400ms frame already matches the settled one. No smooth scroll, pins or sticky elements; a model scale-in keyframe over 1.2s cubic-bezier(.36,.18,0,.99) with a 1.5s glow grows the roaster into place, link underlines wipe in by clip-path over 2.5s, overlay panels slide in over 0.8s, and the most common duration is 0.3s.
